- paseo: Paseo reference for managing agents and worktrees. Load whenever you need to create agents, send them prompts, or manage worktrees.
- paseo-advisor: Spin up a single agent as an advisor — second opinion on the current task. Use when the user says "advisor", "second opinion", "what does X think", or wants an outside take without delegating the work itself.
- paseo-committee: Form a committee of two high-reasoning agents to step back, do root cause analysis, and produce a plan. Use when stuck, looping, tunnel-visioning, or facing a hard planning problem.
- paseo-handoff: Hand off the current task to another agent with full context. Use when the user says "handoff", "hand off", "hand this to", or wants to pass work to another agent.
- paseo-loop: Run an agent loop until an exit condition is met. Use when the user says "loop", "babysit", "keep trying until", "check every X", "watch", or wants iterative autonomous execution.
- skills: Reference codebase for Crates. Use this skill when you need to understand the structure, implementation patterns, or code details of the Crates project.
- zeroclaw: ZeroClaw Quick Reference
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	set -euo pipefail
3	# setup-wg-decoy.sh — Oracle Always Free ARM VM decoy WG ingress
4	#
5	# Architecture:
6	#   Oracle VPS = WG decoy ingress only (handshake + identity injection)
7	#   3tched     = Xray + data plane (WG protocol dropped after identity)
8	#
9	# This script sets up:
10	#   1. WireGuard server listener on port 51821
11	#   2. Identity injection via PostUp (writes WG pubkey to /dev/shm/decoy_identity)
12	#   3. Forwarding rule: after identity check, route to 3tched Xray via WG tunnel
13	#   4. Anti-reclamation keepalive (Oracle reclaims idle <20% for 7 days)
14	#   5. s6 service supervision
15	#
16	# Prerequisites:
17	#   - Oracle Always Free VM.Standard.A1.Flex (Oracle Linux ARM)
18	#   - Root access
19	#   - 3tched's WG pubkey and IP set below
20	
21	# ── Detect distro ─────────────────────────────────────────────
22	if [ -f /etc/oracle-release ]; then
23	    DISTRO="oracle"
24	    PKG_MGR="dnf"
25	elif [ -f /etc/debian_version ]; then
26	    DISTRO="debian"
27	    PKG_MGR="apt"
28	else
29	    DISTRO="unknown"
30	    PKG_MGR="apt"
31	fi
32	
33	# ── Configuration ──────────────────────────────────────────────
34	WG_PORT=51821
35	WG_IFACE=wg0
36	WG_CONF="/etc/wireguard/${WG_IFACE}.conf"
37	WG_NETWORK="10.189.0.0/24"         # decoy WG subnet (separate from 10.200.0.0/24 gRPC)
38	WG_VPS_IP="10.189.0.1/24"
39	
40	# 3tched hypervisor — where Xray lives
41	THREETCHED_WG_PUBKEY=""             # SET: 3tched's WG public key
42	THREETCHED_ENDPOINT=""              # SET: 3tched's public IP:51821 or hostname
43	THREETCHED_WG_IP="10.189.0.2/32"    # 3tched's IP within decoy WG subnet
44	
45	# Identity sled output (consumed by ghostbridge on 3tched)
46	IDENTITY_FILE="/dev/shm/decoy_identity"
47	
48	# Anti-reclamation settings
49	CPU_BURN_SECONDS=5                  # seconds of CPU work per cycle
50	CYCLE_SECONDS=60                    # seconds per keepalive cycle
51	
52	# ── Install packages ─────────────────────────────────────────
53	echo "[decoy] Installing packages on ${DISTRO}..."
54	
55	if [ "$DISTRO" = "oracle" ]; then
56	    # Oracle Linux 8+: WireGuard module is built into kernel (kernel-modules-extra)
57	    dnf install -y wireguard-tools curl jq iptables-services
58	    # Ensure kernel module loaded
59	    modprobe wireguard 2>/dev/null || true
60	    echo "wireguard" > /etc/modules-load.d/wireguard.conf
61	elif [ "$DISTRO" = "debian" ]; then
62	    apt-get update -qq
63	    apt-get install -y -qq wireguard-tools curl jq
64	fi
65	
66	# Generate server keypair if not exists
67	if [ ! -f /etc/wireguard/server_private.key ]; then
68	    wg genkey | tee /etc/wireguard/server_private.key | wg pubkey > /etc/wireguard/server_public.key
69	    chmod 600 /etc/wireguard/server_private.key
70	fi
71	
72	SERVER_PRIVKEY=$(cat /etc/wireguard/server_private.key)
73	SERVER_PUBKEY=$(cat /etc/wireguard/server_public.key)
74	
75	echo "[decoy] Server WG pubkey: ${SERVER_PUBKEY}"
76	
77	# ── Generate WireGuard config ─────────────────────────────────
78	if [ -n "${THREETCHED_WG_PUBKEY}" ] && [ -n "${THREETCHED_ENDPOINT}" ]; then
79	    cat > "${WG_CONF}" <<EOF
80	[Interface]
81	PrivateKey = ${SERVER_PRIVKEY}
82	Address = ${WG_VPS_IP}
83	ListenPort = ${WG_PORT}
84	
85	# Identity injection: log peer pubkey on handshake
86	PostUp = echo "[decoy] WG interface up" && mkdir -p /dev/shm
87	PostUp = wg show ${WG_IFACE} latest-handshakes 2>/dev/null || true
88	
89	# Peer: 3tched hypervisor (Xray data plane)
90	[Peer]
91	PublicKey = ${THREETCHED_WG_PUBKEY}
92	AllowedIPs = ${THREETCHED_WG_IP}
93	Endpoint = ${THREETCHED_ENDPOINT}
94	PersistentKeepalive = 25
95	EOF
96	else
97	    echo "[decoy] WARNING: THREETCHED_WG_PUBKEY/THREETCHED_ENDPOINT not set."
98	    echo "[decoy] Generating server-only config. Add peer manually later."
99	    cat > "${WG_CONF}" <<EOF
100	[Interface]
101	PrivateKey = ${SERVER_PRIVKEY}
102	Address = ${WG_VPS_IP}
103	ListenPort = ${WG_PORT}
104	
105	PostUp = echo "[decoy] WG interface up" && mkdir -p /dev/shm
106	EOF
107	fi
108	
109	chmod 600 "${WG_CONF}"
110	
111	# ── Identity injection watcher ────────────────────────────────
112	mkdir -p /usr/local/sbin
113	
114	cat > /usr/local/sbin/decoy-identity-watcher.sh <<'WATCHER'
115	#!/bin/sh
116	# Watches for WG handshakes and injects identity into /dev/shm/decoy_identity
117	IFACE="${1:-wg0}"
118	IDENTITY_FILE="/dev/shm/decoy_identity"
119	LAST_HANDSHAKE=0
120	
121	while true; do
122	    HANDSHAKE=$(wg show "$IFACE" latest-handshakes 2>/dev/null | head -1)
123	    PUBKEY=$(wg show "$IFACE" peers 2>/dev/null | head -1)
124	
125	    if [ -n "$HANDSHAKE" ] && [ "$HANDSHAKE" != "$LAST_HANDSHAKE" ] && [ -n "$PUBKEY" ]; then
126	        LAST_HANDSHAKE="$HANDSHAKE"
127	        echo "{\"pubkey\":\"${PUBKEY}\",\"timestamp\":\"$(date -Iseconds)\",\"handshake\":\"${HANDSHAKE}\"}" > "$IDENTITY_FILE"
128	        echo "[decoy-identity] Injected identity for peer ${PUBKEY}"
129	    fi
130	    sleep 5
131	done
132	WATCHER
133	chmod +x /usr/local/sbin/decoy-identity-watcher.sh
134	
135	# ── Anti-reclamation keepalive ────────────────────────────────
136	# Oracle reclaims Always Free VMs idle >7 days at <20% CPU/net/mem
137	cat > /usr/local/sbin/decoy-keepalive.sh <<'KEEPALIVE'
138	#!/bin/sh
139	# Anti-reclamation keepalive for Oracle Always Free
140	
141	# Light CPU burn: compress /dev/urandom for a few seconds
142	burn_cpu() {
143	    timeout ${CPU_BURN_SECONDS:-5} sh -c 'cat /dev/urandom | gzip -1 > /dev/null' 2>/dev/null || true
144	}
145	
146	# Light network activity: curl a small endpoint
147	burn_net() {
148	    curl -sf -o /dev/null https://www.microsoft.com/ 2>/dev/null || true
149	    curl -sf -o /dev/null https://www.apple.com/ 2>/dev/null || true
150	}
151	
152	# WG keepalive: send traffic through tunnel if peer exists
153	burn_wg() {

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# setup-wg-decoy.sh — Oracle Always Free ARM VM decoy WG ingress
#
# Architecture:
#   Oracle VPS = WG decoy ingress only (handshake + identity injection)
#   3tched     = Xray + data plane (WG protocol dropped after identity)
#
# This script sets up:
#   1. WireGuard server listener on port 51821
#   2. Identity injection via PostUp (writes WG pubkey to /dev/shm/decoy_identity)
#   3. Forwarding rule: after identity check, route to 3tched Xray via WG tunnel
#   4. Anti-reclamation keepalive (Oracle reclaims idle <20% for 7 days)
#   5. s6 service supervision
#
# Prerequisites:
#   - Oracle Always Free VM.Standard.A1.Flex (Oracle Linux ARM)
#   - Root access
#   - 3tched's WG pubkey and IP set below

# ── Detect distro ─────────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -f /etc/oracle-release ]; then
    DISTRO="oracle"
    PKG_MGR="dnf"
elif [ -f /etc/debian_version ]; then
    DISTRO="debian"
    PKG_MGR="apt"
else
    DISTRO="unknown"
    PKG_MGR="apt"
fi

# ── Configuration ──────────────────────────────────────────────
WG_PORT=51821
WG_IFACE=wg0
WG_CONF="/etc/wireguard/${WG_IFACE}.conf"
WG_NETWORK="10.189.0.0/24"         # decoy WG subnet (separate from 10.200.0.0/24 gRPC)
WG_VPS_IP="10.189.0.1/24"

# 3tched hypervisor — where Xray lives
THREETCHED_WG_PUBKEY=""             # SET: 3tched's WG public key
THREETCHED_ENDPOINT=""              # SET: 3tched's public IP:51821 or hostname
THREETCHED_WG_IP="10.189.0.2/32"    # 3tched's IP within decoy WG subnet

# Identity sled output (consumed by ghostbridge on 3tched)
IDENTITY_FILE="/dev/shm/decoy_identity"

# Anti-reclamation settings
CPU_BURN_SECONDS=5                  # seconds of CPU work per cycle
CYCLE_SECONDS=60                    # seconds per keepalive cycle

# ── Install packages ─────────────────────────────────────────
echo "[decoy] Installing packages on ${DISTRO}..."

if [ "$DISTRO" = "oracle" ]; then
    # Oracle Linux 8+: WireGuard module is built into kernel (kernel-modules-extra)
    dnf install -y wireguard-tools curl jq iptables-services
    # Ensure kernel module loaded
    modprobe wireguard 2>/dev/null || true
    echo "wireguard" > /etc/modules-load.d/wireguard.conf
elif [ "$DISTRO" = "debian" ]; then
    apt-get update -qq
    apt-get install -y -qq wireguard-tools curl jq
fi

# Generate server keypair if not exists
if [ ! -f /etc/wireguard/server_private.key ]; then
    wg genkey | tee /etc/wireguard/server_private.key | wg pubkey > /etc/wireguard/server_public.key
    chmod 600 /etc/wireguard/server_private.key
fi

SERVER_PRIVKEY=$(cat /etc/wireguard/server_private.key)
SERVER_PUBKEY=$(cat /etc/wireguard/server_public.key)

echo "[decoy] Server WG pubkey: ${SERVER_PUBKEY}"

# ── Generate WireGuard config ─────────────────────────────────
if [ -n "${THREETCHED_WG_PUBKEY}" ] && [ -n "${THREETCHED_ENDPOINT}" ]; then
    cat > "${WG_CONF}" <<EOF
[Interface]
PrivateKey = ${SERVER_PRIVKEY}
Address = ${WG_VPS_IP}
ListenPort = ${WG_PORT}

# Identity injection: log peer pubkey on handshake
PostUp = echo "[decoy] WG interface up" && mkdir -p /dev/shm
PostUp = wg show ${WG_IFACE} latest-handshakes 2>/dev/null || true

# Peer: 3tched hypervisor (Xray data plane)
[Peer]
PublicKey = ${THREETCHED_WG_PUBKEY}
AllowedIPs = ${THREETCHED_WG_IP}
Endpoint = ${THREETCHED_ENDPOINT}
PersistentKeepalive = 25
EOF
else
    echo "[decoy] WARNING: THREETCHED_WG_PUBKEY/THREETCHED_ENDPOINT not set."
    echo "[decoy] Generating server-only config. Add peer manually later."
    cat > "${WG_CONF}" <<EOF
[Interface]
PrivateKey = ${SERVER_PRIVKEY}
Address = ${WG_VPS_IP}
ListenPort = ${WG_PORT}

PostUp = echo "[decoy] WG interface up" && mkdir -p /dev/shm
EOF
fi

chmod 600 "${WG_CONF}"

# ── Identity injection watcher ────────────────────────────────
mkdir -p /usr/local/sbin

cat > /usr/local/sbin/decoy-identity-watcher.sh <<'WATCHER'
#!/bin/sh
# Watches for WG handshakes and injects identity into /dev/shm/decoy_identity
IFACE="${1:-wg0}"
IDENTITY_FILE="/dev/shm/decoy_identity"
LAST_HANDSHAKE=0

while true; do
    HANDSHAKE=$(wg show "$IFACE" latest-handshakes 2>/dev/null | head -1)
    PUBKEY=$(wg show "$IFACE" peers 2>/dev/null | head -1)

    if [ -n "$HANDSHAKE" ] && [ "$HANDSHAKE" != "$LAST_HANDSHAKE" ] && [ -n "$PUBKEY" ]; then
        LAST_HANDSHAKE="$HANDSHAKE"
        echo "{\"pubkey\":\"${PUBKEY}\",\"timestamp\":\"$(date -Iseconds)\",\"handshake\":\"${HANDSHAKE}\"}" > "$IDENTITY_FILE"
        echo "[decoy-identity] Injected identity for peer ${PUBKEY}"
    fi
    sleep 5
done
WATCHER
chmod +x /usr/local/sbin/decoy-identity-watcher.sh

# ── Anti-reclamation keepalive ────────────────────────────────
# Oracle reclaims Always Free VMs idle >7 days at <20% CPU/net/mem
cat > /usr/local/sbin/decoy-keepalive.sh <<'KEEPALIVE'
#!/bin/sh
# Anti-reclamation keepalive for Oracle Always Free

# Light CPU burn: compress /dev/urandom for a few seconds
burn_cpu() {
    timeout ${CPU_BURN_SECONDS:-5} sh -c 'cat /dev/urandom | gzip -1 > /dev/null' 2>/dev/null || true
}

# Light network activity: curl a small endpoint
burn_net() {
    curl -sf -o /dev/null https://www.microsoft.com/ 2>/dev/null || true
    curl -sf -o /dev/null https://www.apple.com/ 2>/dev/null || true
}

# WG keepalive: send traffic through tunnel if peer exists
burn_wg() {
    IFACE="${1:-wg0}"
    PEER_IP=$(wg show "$IFACE" allowed-ips 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $2}' | head -1)
    if [ -n "$PEER_IP" ] && [ "$PEER_IP" != "(none)" ]; then
        ping -c 1 -W 2 "${PEER_IP%%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
}

CYCLE="${CYCLE_SECONDS:-60}"
echo "[keepalive] Starting anti-reclamation loop (cycle=${CYCLE}s)"

while true; do
    burn_cpu
    burn_net
    burn_wg "${1:-wg0}"
    sleep "$CYCLE"
done
KEEPALIVE
chmod +x /usr/local/sbin/decoy-keepalive.sh

# ── s6 service supervision ───────────────────────────────────
if ! command -v s6-svc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "[decoy] Installing s6..."
    if [ "$DISTRO" = "oracle" ]; then
        # Build s6 from source on Oracle Linux
        S6_VER="2.13.1.0"
        SKALIBS_VER="2.14.1.1"
        EXECLINE_VER="2.9.6.1"
        TMP="/tmp/s6-build"
        mkdir -p "$TMP"
        for pkg in skalibs execline s6; do
            ver=""
            [ "$pkg" = "skalibs" ] && ver="$SKALIBS_VER"
            [ "$pkg" = "execline" ] && ver="$EXECLINE_VER"
            [ "$pkg" = "s6" ] && ver="$S6_VER"
            curl -sL "https://skarnet.org/software/${pkg}/${pkg}-${ver}.tar.gz" | tar xz -C "$TMP"
            cd "${TMP}/${pkg}-${ver}"
            ./configure --prefix=/usr --disable-shared --libdir=/usr/lib64
            make -j$(nproc) && make install
        done
        cd -
    elif [ "$DISTRO" = "debian" ]; then
        apt-get install -y -qq s6 || {
            # Same source build fallback
            S6_VER="2.13.1.0"
            SKALIBS_VER="2.14.1.1"
            EXECLINE_VER="2.9.6.1"
            TMP="/tmp/s6-build"
            mkdir -p "$TMP"
            for pkg in skalibs execline s6; do
                ver=""
                [ "$pkg" = "skalibs" ] && ver="$SKALIBS_VER"
                [ "$pkg" = "execline" ] && ver="$EXECLINE_VER"
                [ "$pkg" = "s6" ] && ver="$S6_VER"
                curl -sL "https://skarnet.org/software/${pkg}/${pkg}-${ver}.tar.gz" | tar xz -C "$TMP"
                cd "${TMP}/${pkg}-${ver}"
                ./configure --prefix=/usr --disable-shared
                make -j$(nproc) && make install
            done
            cd -
        }
    fi
fi

S6_SVDIR="/etc/s6/sv"
S6_DIR="${S6_SVDIR}/decoy-wg"

mkdir -p "${S6_DIR}"
cat > "${S6_DIR}/run" <<'S6RUN'
#!/bin/sh
exec 2>&1
IFACE="${IFACE:-wg0}"
CONF="${WG_CONF:-/etc/wireguard/wg0.conf}"

if [ ! -f "$CONF" ]; then
    echo "[decoy-wg] No config at $CONF, exiting"
    exit 0
fi

wg-quick up "$IFACE" 2>/dev/null || true
echo "[decoy-wg] WireGuard up on ${IFACE}"

for _ in $(seq 1 10); do
    ip link show "$IFACE" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
    sleep 1
done

/usr/local/sbin/decoy-identity-watcher.sh "$IFACE" &
IDENTITY_PID=$!

/usr/local/sbin/decoy-keepalive.sh "$IFACE" &
KEEPALIVE_PID=$!

wait -n 2>/dev/null || wait

kill "$IDENTITY_PID" "$KEEPALIVE_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
wg-quick down "$IFACE" 2>/dev/null || true
S6RUN
chmod +x "${S6_DIR}/run"

cat > "${S6_DIR}/finish" <<'S6FIN'
#!/bin/sh
exec 2>&1
IFACE="${IFACE:-wg0}"
wg-quick down "$IFACE" 2>/dev/null || true
echo "[decoy-wg] WireGuard down"
S6FIN
chmod +x "${S6_DIR}/finish"

echo "longrun" > "${S6_DIR}/type"

# ── Firewall ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
if [ "$DISTRO" = "oracle" ]; then
    # Oracle Linux uses iptables/firewalld
    if systemctl is-active firewalld >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port="${WG_PORT}/udp"
        firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=22/tcp
        firewall-cmd --reload
    else
        iptables -A INPUT -p udp --dport "${WG_PORT}" -j ACCEPT
        iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
        iptables -A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
        iptables -P INPUT DROP
        iptables-save > /etc/sysconfig/iptables 2>/dev/null || true
        systemctl enable iptables 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
elif command -v ufw >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ufw allow "${WG_PORT}/udp" comment "WG decoy ingress"
    ufw allow 22/tcp comment "SSH"
    ufw --force enable
fi

# ── Start ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo ""
echo "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
echo "  Oracle Decoy WG Ingress — Setup Complete"
echo "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
echo ""
echo "  Server WG Pubkey: ${SERVER_PUBKEY}"
echo "  Listen Port:      ${WG_PORT}"
echo "  WG Subnet:        ${WG_NETWORK}"
echo "  Identity File:    ${IDENTITY_FILE}"
echo "  Distro:           ${DISTRO}"
echo ""
echo "  NEXT STEPS:"
echo "  1. Set THREETCHED_WG_PUBKEY and THREETCHED_ENDPOINT above"
echo "  2. Re-run this script or edit ${WG_CONF} manually"
echo "  3. On 3tched, add this server as a WG peer:"
echo "     PublicKey = ${SERVER_PUBKEY}"
echo "     Endpoint = <ORACLE_VPS_IP>:${WG_PORT}"
echo "     AllowedIPs = 10.189.0.1/32"
echo "  4. Start: wg-quick up ${WG_IFACE}"
echo "     Or via s6: s6-svc -u ${S6_DIR}"
echo ""

1	# Public Domain Setup Guide
2	
3	## Quick Setup (Recommended)
4	
5	```bash
6	cd /home/jeremy/op-dbus-v2/deploy
7	./setup-public-domain.sh
8	```
9	
10	This will:
11	1. Install Caddy or Nginx
12	2. Configure automatic HTTPS
13	3. Set up systemd service
14	4. Configure firewall
15	5. Start the service
16	
17	## Prerequisites
18	
19	### 1. Domain Name
20	- Register a domain (e.g., from Cloudflare, Namecheap, GoDaddy)
21	- Point DNS A record to your server's public IP
22	
23	Check your public IP:
24	```bash
25	curl -4 ifconfig.me
26	```
27	
28	### 2. DNS Configuration
29	Add these records at your DNS provider:
30	
31	```
32	Type    Name    Value               TTL
33	A       chat    YOUR_SERVER_IP      300
34	A       @       YOUR_SERVER_IP      300  (if you want root domain)
35	```
36	
37	Wait 5-10 minutes for DNS propagation. Verify:
38	```bash
39	dig chat.yourdomain.com
40	nslookup chat.yourdomain.com
41	```
42	
43	### 3. Server Requirements
44	- Public IP address
45	- Ports 80 and 443 open (firewall/cloud security group)
46	- Root or sudo access
47	
48	## Manual Setup Options
49	
50	### Option A: Caddy (Easiest - Auto HTTPS)
51	
52	#### Install Caddy
53	```bash
54	sudo apt install -y debian-keyring debian-archive-keyring apt-transport-https curl
55	curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/gpg.key' | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/caddy-stable-archive-keyring.gpg
56	curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/debian.deb.txt' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/caddy-stable.list
57	sudo apt update
58	sudo apt install -y caddy
59	```
60	
61	#### Configure
62	```bash
63	# Edit Caddyfile
64	sudo nano /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
65	
66	# Replace DOMAIN with your actual domain:
67	chat.yourdomain.com {
68	    reverse_proxy localhost:8080
69	}
70	```
71	
72	#### Start
73	```bash
74	sudo systemctl restart caddy
75	sudo systemctl enable caddy
76	```
77	
78	**That's it!** Caddy automatically gets Let's Encrypt certificates.
79	
80	### Option B: Nginx + Certbot
81	
82	#### Install
83	```bash
84	sudo apt update
85	sudo apt install -y nginx certbot python3-certbot-nginx
86	```
87	
88	#### Configure
89	```bash
90	# Copy config
91	sudo cp /home/jeremy/op-dbus-v2/deploy/nginx/op-web.conf /etc/nginx/sites-available/
92	
93	# Edit domain name
94	sudo nano /etc/nginx/sites-available/op-web.conf
95	# Replace all instances of "your-domain.com" with your actual domain
96	
97	# Enable site
98	sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/op-web.conf /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/
99	sudo nginx -t
100	sudo systemctl reload nginx
101	```
102	
103	#### Get SSL Certificate
104	```bash
105	sudo certbot --nginx -d chat.yourdomain.com
106	```
107	
108	Certbot will:
109	- Verify domain ownership
110	- Get SSL certificate
111	- Auto-configure nginx
112	- Set up auto-renewal
113	
114	### Option C: Cloudflare Tunnel (No Public IP Needed!)
115	
116	If you can't open ports or don't have a static IP:
117	
118	#### Install Cloudflared
119	```bash
120	curl -L https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared/releases/latest/download/cloudflared-linux-amd64.deb -o cloudflared.deb
121	sudo dpkg -i cloudflared.deb
122	```
123	
124	#### Authenticate
125	```bash
126	cloudflared tunnel login
127	```
128	
129	#### Create Tunnel
130	```bash
131	cloudflared tunnel create op-web
132	cloudflared tunnel route dns op-web chat.yourdomain.com
133	```
134	
135	#### Configure
136	```bash
137	mkdir -p ~/.cloudflared
138	cat > ~/.cloudflared/config.yml << EOF
139	tunnel: op-web
140	credentials-file: /home/jeremy/.cloudflared/<TUNNEL-ID>.json
141	
142	ingress:
143	  - hostname: chat.yourdomain.com
144	    service: http://localhost:8080
145	  - service: http_status:404
146	EOF
147	```
148	
149	#### Run as Service
150	```bash
151	sudo cloudflared service install
152	sudo systemctl start cloudflared
153	sudo systemctl enable cloudflared
154	```
155	
156	## Systemd Service Setup
157	
158	### Install Service
159	```bash
160	sudo cp /home/jeremy/op-dbus-v2/deploy/systemd/op-web.service /etc/systemd/system/
161	sudo systemctl daemon-reload
162	sudo systemctl enable op-web
163	sudo systemctl start op-web
164	```
165	
166	### Check Status
167	```bash
168	sudo systemctl status op-web
169	sudo journalctl -u op-web -f
170	```
171	
172	### Service Commands
173	```bash
174	sudo systemctl start op-web      # Start
175	sudo systemctl stop op-web       # Stop
176	sudo systemctl restart op-web    # Restart
177	sudo systemctl status op-web     # Status
178	sudo journalctl -u op-web -f     # Live logs
179	```
180

# Public Domain Setup Guide

## Quick Setup (Recommended)

```bash
cd /home/jeremy/op-dbus-v2/deploy
./setup-public-domain.sh
```

This will:
1. Install Caddy or Nginx
2. Configure automatic HTTPS
3. Set up systemd service
4. Configure firewall
5. Start the service

## Prerequisites

### 1. Domain Name
- Register a domain (e.g., from Cloudflare, Namecheap, GoDaddy)
- Point DNS A record to your server's public IP

Check your public IP:
```bash
curl -4 ifconfig.me
```

### 2. DNS Configuration
Add these records at your DNS provider:

```
Type    Name    Value               TTL
A       chat    YOUR_SERVER_IP      300
A       @       YOUR_SERVER_IP      300  (if you want root domain)
```

Wait 5-10 minutes for DNS propagation. Verify:
```bash
dig chat.yourdomain.com
nslookup chat.yourdomain.com
```

### 3. Server Requirements
- Public IP address
- Ports 80 and 443 open (firewall/cloud security group)
- Root or sudo access

## Manual Setup Options

### Option A: Caddy (Easiest - Auto HTTPS)

#### Install Caddy
```bash
sudo apt install -y debian-keyring debian-archive-keyring apt-transport-https curl
curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/gpg.key' | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/caddy-stable-archive-keyring.gpg
curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/debian.deb.txt' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/caddy-stable.list
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y caddy
```

#### Configure
```bash
# Edit Caddyfile
sudo nano /etc/caddy/Caddyfile

# Replace DOMAIN with your actual domain:
chat.yourdomain.com {
    reverse_proxy localhost:8080
}
```

#### Start
```bash
sudo systemctl restart caddy
sudo systemctl enable caddy
```

**That's it!** Caddy automatically gets Let's Encrypt certificates.

### Option B: Nginx + Certbot

#### Install
```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y nginx certbot python3-certbot-nginx
```

#### Configure
```bash
# Copy config
sudo cp /home/jeremy/op-dbus-v2/deploy/nginx/op-web.conf /etc/nginx/sites-available/

# Edit domain name
sudo nano /etc/nginx/sites-available/op-web.conf
# Replace all instances of "your-domain.com" with your actual domain

# Enable site
sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/op-web.conf /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/
sudo nginx -t
sudo systemctl reload nginx
```

#### Get SSL Certificate
```bash
sudo certbot --nginx -d chat.yourdomain.com
```

Certbot will:
- Verify domain ownership
- Get SSL certificate
- Auto-configure nginx
- Set up auto-renewal

### Option C: Cloudflare Tunnel (No Public IP Needed!)

If you can't open ports or don't have a static IP:

#### Install Cloudflared
```bash
curl -L https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared/releases/latest/download/cloudflared-linux-amd64.deb -o cloudflared.deb
sudo dpkg -i cloudflared.deb
```

#### Authenticate
```bash
cloudflared tunnel login
```

#### Create Tunnel
```bash
cloudflared tunnel create op-web
cloudflared tunnel route dns op-web chat.yourdomain.com
```

#### Configure
```bash
mkdir -p ~/.cloudflared
cat > ~/.cloudflared/config.yml << EOF
tunnel: op-web
credentials-file: /home/jeremy/.cloudflared/<TUNNEL-ID>.json

ingress:
  - hostname: chat.yourdomain.com
    service: http://localhost:8080
  - service: http_status:404
EOF
```

#### Run as Service
```bash
sudo cloudflared service install
sudo systemctl start cloudflared
sudo systemctl enable cloudflared
```

## Systemd Service Setup

### Install Service
```bash
sudo cp /home/jeremy/op-dbus-v2/deploy/systemd/op-web.service /etc/systemd/system/
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable op-web
sudo systemctl start op-web
```

### Check Status
```bash
sudo systemctl status op-web
sudo journalctl -u op-web -f
```

### Service Commands
```bash
sudo systemctl start op-web      # Start
sudo systemctl stop op-web       # Stop
sudo systemctl restart op-web    # Restart
sudo systemctl status op-web     # Status
sudo journalctl -u op-web -f     # Live logs
```

## Security Considerations

### 1. Add Authentication (Recommended for Public)

#### Caddy Basic Auth
```bash
# Generate password hash
caddy hash-password

# Add to Caddyfile:
chat.yourdomain.com {
    basicauth /* {
        admin $2a$14$...your-hash-here...
    }
    reverse_proxy localhost:8080
}
```

#### Nginx Basic Auth
```bash
# Create password file
sudo apt install apache2-utils
sudo htpasswd -c /etc/nginx/.htpasswd admin

# Add to nginx config:
location / {
    auth_basic "Restricted Access";
    auth_basic_user_file /etc/nginx/.htpasswd;
    proxy_pass http://localhost:8080;
}
```

### 2. Firewall Setup

#### UFW
```bash
sudo ufw allow 22/tcp   # SSH (don't lock yourself out!)
sudo ufw allow 80/tcp   # HTTP
sudo ufw allow 443/tcp  # HTTPS
sudo ufw enable
```

#### Firewalld
```bash
sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-service=ssh
sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-service=http
sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-service=https
sudo firewall-cmd --reload
```

### 3. Rate Limiting

Already configured in nginx/caddy configs:
- API: 10 requests/second
- Chat: 5 requests/second
- Burst allowance for normal usage

### 4. SSL/TLS Security

Both configs use:
- TLS 1.2 and 1.3 only
- Strong cipher suites
- HSTS headers
- Security headers (XSS, frame options, etc.)

## Monitoring

### Health Check
```bash
curl https://chat.yourdomain.com/api/health
```

### Logs
```bash
# Application logs
sudo journalctl -u op-web -f

# Nginx logs
sudo tail -f /var/log/nginx/op-web-access.log
sudo tail -f /var/log/nginx/op-web-error.log

# Caddy logs
sudo journalctl -u caddy -f
sudo tail -f /var/log/caddy/op-web-access.log
```

## Troubleshooting

### Service won't start
```bash
# Check logs
sudo journalctl -u op-web -n 100

# Check if binary exists
ls -la /home/jeremy/op-dbus-v2/target/release/op-web-server

# Check permissions
sudo systemctl status op-web
```

### SSL certificate fails
```bash
# Check DNS
dig chat.yourdomain.com

# Test certbot
sudo certbot certificates
sudo certbot renew --dry-run

# Check port 80 is open
sudo netstat -tlnp | grep :80
```

### Can't connect to server
```bash
# Check firewall
sudo ufw status
sudo firewall-cmd --list-all

# Check nginx/caddy
sudo systemctl status nginx
sudo systemctl status caddy

# Check op-web
sudo systemctl status op-web
curl http://localhost:8080/api/health
```

### WebSocket not working
- Check proxy config has `Upgrade` and `Connection` headers
- Verify nginx/caddy is passing WebSocket traffic
- Check browser console for errors

## Architecture

```
Internet
   ↓
DNS (chat.yourdomain.com)
   ↓
Firewall (ports 80, 443)
   ↓
Reverse Proxy (Caddy/Nginx)
   ├── SSL/TLS termination
   ├── Rate limiting
   ├── Security headers
   └── WebSocket support
       ↓
   op-web-server (localhost:8080)
       ├── HTTP server
       ├── WebSocket handler
       ├── Chat orchestrator
       └── Tool registry
```

## Quick Commands Reference

```bash
# Setup (automated)
./deploy/setup-public-domain.sh

# Manual service control
sudo systemctl start op-web
sudo systemctl status op-web
sudo systemctl restart op-web
sudo journalctl -u op-web -f

# Web server control
sudo systemctl restart caddy  # or nginx
sudo systemctl status caddy   # or nginx

# Check if site is accessible
curl -I https://chat.yourdomain.com

# View SSL certificate
echo | openssl s_client -connect chat.yourdomain.com:443 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -text

# Test health endpoint
curl https://chat.yourdomain.com/api/health
```

## Cost-Free Options

### Free Domains
- Freenom (free .tk, .ml, .ga domains)
- DuckDNS (free subdomain)
- No-IP (free subdomain)

### Free SSL
- Let's Encrypt (automated with Caddy/Certbot)
- Cloudflare (automatic with Cloudflare Tunnel)

### Free Hosting
- Run on existing server
- Oracle Cloud free tier
- Google Cloud free tier
- AWS free tier (12 months)

## Next Steps

1. ✅ Run setup script
2. ✅ Verify DNS points to your server
3. ✅ Access https://chat.yourdomain.com/chat.html
4. ⚠️  Add authentication for public access
5. 📊 Set up monitoring/alerting
6. 🔐 Review security best practices

# OP-DBUS ingress lockdown — the oracle WireGuard tunnel is the ONLY entry.
#
# Composes with the fail2ban (ip filter) and incus (inet incus) tables:
# nftables drops a packet if ANY base chain drops it, so this table's drop
# policy is authoritative regardless of their accept policies.
#
# Entry model:
#   - opdbus (WG, 10.0.0.0/24)  = the identity plane; SSH, xray, everything.
#   - WG handshakes (udp 51823) accepted from the oracle decoy VPS only.
#   - ovsbr0                    = container mgmt bridge (dnsmasq, incusd, op-dbus gRPC).
#   - Public NIC (eth0)         = no service reachable; conntrack replies + DHCP only.

add table inet lockdown
flush table inet lockdown

table inet lockdown {
    define ORACLE_DECOY = 129.153.134.63
    define WG_PORT = 51823

    chain input {
        type filter hook input priority -10; policy drop;

        iif "lo" accept
        ct state established,related accept
        ct state invalid drop

        # The identity plane: everything rides the oracle WG tunnel.
        iifname "opdbus" accept

        # Container/management bridge stays internal.
        iifname "ovsbr0" accept

        # WG handshakes only from the oracle decoy ingress.
        ip saddr $ORACLE_DECOY udp dport $WG_PORT accept

        # DHCP lease renewal on the uplink.
        udp sport 67 udp dport 68 accept

        # IPv6 liveness (NDP); echo only via the tunnel (covered by opdbus).
        icmpv6 type { nd-neighbor-solicit, nd-neighbor-advert, nd-router-advert, nd-router-solicit } accept
    }
}

# Oracle Decoy Ingress — UDP Relay Mode (Handoff)

Decision made 2026-07-07: **relay, not terminate.** The oracle VPS forwards raw
WireGuard UDP packets to 3tched; it never holds a WG private key for the
opdbus interface. This keeps the pubkey→Argon2(PSK, salt=pubkey) sessionid
chain end-to-end — oracle is ingress-only, never an identity party. See
`project_container_identity_is_sessionid` / `project_key_derivation` memory
for why terminating on oracle would break that chain (3tched would see
oracle's key, not the client's).

## Current live state (this host, "3tched")

```
interface: opdbus            (WG_PORT 51823)
peer: 6mx4yc...  (ORACLE)     endpoint 129.153.134.63:51821, allowed 10.0.0.0/24
peer: OpczuI...  (direct-in)  no endpoint set, allowed 10.0.0.3/32
```

- 3tched dials **out** to the oracle peer (keepalive-driven), so that peer
  needs no firewall change here.
- The `OpczuI...` peer currently has **no endpoint** — it dials 3tched's
  public IP (148.113.204.83:51823) directly. That direct path is exactly the
  "theater" being closed off.

## Firewall on 3tched (already staged, not yet applied)

`/etc/nftables-lockdown.nft` — default-drop on all input except loopback,
established/related, the `opdbus` and `ovsbr0` interfaces, and inbound WG
handshakes from `129.153.134.63` on udp/51823. Once applied, direct clients
hitting 148.113.204.83:51823 from any other source IP are dropped. Not yet
run (`nft -f /etc/nftables-lockdown.nft`) — pending your go-ahead per the
plan.

## Oracle side: what to add (relay, no key material)

On the oracle decoy VPS, add a stateless UDP DNAT so port 51821 (public)
forwards straight through to 3tched's real WG port, with no WG stack of its
own involved in the client-facing hop:

```bash
# oracle VPS — nftables DNAT relay, no WireGuard interface needed here
nft add table ip relay
nft add chain ip relay prerouting  '{ type nat hook prerouting priority -100 ; }'
nft add chain ip relay postrouting '{ type nat hook postrouting priority 100 ; }'

nft add rule ip relay prerouting udp dport 51821 dnat to 148.113.204.83:51823
nft add rule ip relay postrouting ip daddr 148.113.204.83 udp dport 51823 masquerade

sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
echo 'net.ipv4.ip_forward=1' >> /etc/sysctl.conf
```

This replaces the WG-server config `setup-wg-decoy.sh` currently sketches
(that script stands up a full `wg0` interface + peer table on oracle — that
is **termination mode**, option 2 from the earlier analysis, and should not
be run as-is now that relay was chosen). Keep the script around as a
reference for anti-reclamation keepalive / s6 supervision ideas, but the
`[Interface]`/`[Peer]` WG config block it generates should not be deployed.

## Client conf change (only for direct-dial peers)

Any peer whose `[Peer]` block currently has no `Endpoint` (i.e. relies on
dialing 3tched's public IP directly, like `OpczuI...`) needs one line added:

```ini
[Peer]
PublicKey = <3tched pubkey: iNqgBk7pBC/iXUmF+v4PNvvdAxjP5qWjxzMYYRE8+hw=>
Endpoint = 129.153.134.63:51821
AllowedIPs = 10.0.0.0/24
```

Keypairs are unchanged — only the endpoint moves from 3tched's public IP to
the oracle relay IP:port. The oracle peer itself (already endpoint-configured
at 129.153.134.63:51821) needs no change.

## Remaining steps (plan tracker)

1. Apply oracle-side DNAT rule above.
2. Update direct-dial client(s) to the new `Endpoint`; confirm handshake
   still completes through the relay.
3. Apply `/etc/nftables-lockdown.nft` on 3tched (`nft -f ...`), verify oracle
   handshake and container/bridge traffic (ovsbr0, incus) still work.
4. Persist both rulesets: 3tched lockdown via whatever loads nftables at
   boot on this Artix box (s6 service, not systemd — check `/etc/s6/sv` for
   an existing nftables unit before adding one); oracle side likewise via its
   own init (this box is systemd/Oracle Linux, so a plain `nftables.service`
   load of a saved ruleset file is normal there).

# Ghostbridge Identity Sled + Snowball Accountability Pipeline (Recovered + As-Built)

**Status**: Long-standing core architecture. Design artifacts partially erased in 783dced7; implementation and intent preserved in code and recoverable commits.

**Date of recovery**: 2026-07-03 (from pre-783dced7 .kiro specs + live sources).

## Core Principle (Absolute Base)

`PluginSchema` is the single source of truth.
No valid schema => entity does not exist on the system.

Identity, mutations, traces, and accountability are always bound to the current schema state via a cryptographic footprint.

## The Model (Settled)

- **Identity is the WireGuard public key** (Curve25519). It is persistent for the account lifetime.
- **The Sled** (`/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat`) is a `#[repr(C)]` 152-byte structure (IdentitySled):
  - `wireguard_pubkey: [u8; 32]`
  - `mutation_index: u64`
  - `hashed_footprint: [u8; 32]` (Blake3)
  - `trace_id: [u8; 16]`
  - `schema_version`, `vector_id` (Qdrant episode), reserved.
- **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (`op-identity/src/anna_scribe.rs`): Notarizes arrival. On WireGuard identity presentation:
  - Performs 1:1 direct read of the sled.
  - Validates sled (non-zero footprint + trace_id).
  - Does the **Strike/Etch**: blake3(wg_pubkey + schema_catalog_blob + mutation_index).
  - Produces genesis **Snowball** ledger entry (`SessionLedger`).
- **The Shuttle / Schema Bridge** (`op-identity/src/schema_bridge.rs`):
  - SchemaEngine writes the sled on relevant schema mutations (zero-copy / tmpfs only).
  - Readers (Shuttle) mmap once, cast, extract `GB_FOOTPRINT` / `GB_TRACE_ID` (optionally WG pubkey) into env.
  - Writes stateless Xray config (`/dev/shm/xray-ghostbridge.json`) and hands off.
  - Strictly avoids any disk I/O that would hit Btrfs.
- **Xray** (in the wg-xray datapath):
  - Receives GB_* env vars.
  - Injects into gRPC metadata on outbound:
    - `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint`
    - `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID`
    - `X-WireGuard-Pubkey` (when applicable).
- **GhostbridgeInterceptor** (`op-grpc-bridge/src/interceptor.rs` + similar in other crates):
  - Enforces the Accountability Loop on every gRPC ingress (port 18789).
  - Requires the two Ghostbridge headers.
  - Re-reads the live sled (zero-copy).
  - Rejects on:
    - Missing headers.
    - Invalid sled state (per Absolute Base).
    - Footprint mismatch (client out of sync with current mutation_index / Btrfs state).
  - Passes validated `trace_id` downstream via request extensions for GUI / Qdrant linkage.
- **Snowball Session Ledger**: Appended audit chain starting with the genesis record from A.N.N.A. Scribe. Lives in shared memory; can be streamed / projected.

Mutations that change schema state update `mutation_index` + footprint. Every subsequent call carries a fresh proof that the client is synchronized with the authoritative mutation history.

## Relation to PluginSchema and Blobs (2026 evolution)

- The sled/footprint **binds identity to the schema state** (hash of canonicalized PluginSchema / catalog).
- Modern bridge uses **per-plugin `PluginObjectBlob`** (see `docs/schema-coupled-plugin-blob-reflection-whitepaper.md`).
- Blobs copy `D-Bus identity + gRPC identity + method metadata from PluginSchema.methods`.
- Restoration of typed `MethodDecl`, `SideEffect`, `SignalDecl`, etc. (from earlier recovery of op-state-store/plugin_schema) directly feeds richer blob synthesis and reflection.

## Key Invariants (AGENTS + recovered specs)

- D-Bus is the only control plane.
- 1:1 direct read (zero-copy mmap in /dev/shm) — no SQL polling, no generic D-Bus watchers for state.
- Zero-Btrfs overhead for the identity/accountability path (NVMe preserved for blockchain vectorized transport).
- Schema drives everything: if no valid PluginSchema, no identity, no service, nothing exists.
- Persistent WG-key identity (account lifetime), not ephemeral SQL sessions.
- Full accountability loop: WG handshake → AnnaScribe Snowball → Xray header injection → Interceptor enforcement → trace propagation.

## Recovered Artifacts (from 783dced7^)

- `.kiro/specs/3tched-schema-shuttle-xray-pipeline/{design,requirements,tasks}.md`
  - Detailed phased implementation (Sled struct/layout, Shuttle zero-copy + env injection + disk-I/O abort, GhostbridgeInterceptor, JSON-RPC Mutation Pipeline stages, AI Accountability).
- Consistent terminology: The Sled, The Shuttle, Strike/Etch, The Snowball, A.N.N.A. Scribe, Accountability Loop, Absolute Base.

Current code in `op-identity`, `op-grpc-bridge`, `op-projection`, `op-cognitive-mcp`, etc. implements the above with only minor natural extensions (Qdrant vector_id, subid taxonomy, per-object blobs).

## Current Primary Files (as-built)

aiTitle: Lockdown operation-dbus firewall with oracle WireGuard relay

content.text:
This clarifies everything. Oracle already runs a full WG hub (`wg0`, port 51821) with 3 peers:

1. **`iNqgBk…hw=`** = 3tched itself (endpoint `148.113.204.83:51823`, `10.0.0.2/32`) — fresh handshake, this is the legitimate backhaul.
2. **`BhFpz…7c2U=`** = allowed `10.0.0.3/32`, endpoint **`97.221.194.121:51821`** — that's *your current SSH client IP*. Your laptop is already correctly connecting through oracle's hub, fresh handshake, and oracle's existing DNAT/FORWARD rules already route its traffic to the right TCP ports on 3tched. This part of the design is done and working (57GB+ transferred).
3. **`DHLZcb…TAs=`** — `10.189.0.2/32`, port 51876, handshake 24 days stale — leftover from the older separate decoy scheme in `setup-wg-decoy.sh` (different subnet, different port). Dead weight, not urgent.

So the oracle-side relay was never missing — no new work needed there. The actual dangling piece is on **3tched's own `opdbus` interface**: the `OpczuI…Ehm=` peer (also claiming `10.0.0.3/32`, no endpoint, handshake always `0`) is a stale, unused, duplicate entry — a second, direct-dial path to the same address your real client already reaches properly through oracle. Nobody's using it (handshake never completed). It's the literal "theater" surface, now blocked by the lockdown but still sitting in the config.

Want me to remove that dead `OpczuI…` peer from 3tched's `opdbus` WG config? It's unused, so this should be a no-op for anyone actually connected — just closes the redundant entry for good instead of relying on the firewall alone.

623	/// Build the Xray config JSON as a string (pure — no I/O).
624	///
625	/// Routes are sourced from Gemma (`/dev/shm/xray-routes.json`) and merged with
626	/// legacy `UNIX_SOCKET_ENDPOINTS` entries.  Gemma routes take precedence; legacy
627	/// sockets are only added when no Gemma route has the same tag.  The final
628	/// catch-all rule sends unmatched ingress traffic to the grpc-bridge, matching
629	/// the historical fallback behavior.
630	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
631	fn build_xray_config(
632	    footprint: &str,
633	    trace_id: &str,
634	    nextdns_profile: &str,
635	    uuid: &str,
636	    private_key: &str,
637	    short_id: &str,
638	    sockets: &[SocketEntry],
639	    routes: &[XrayRoute],
640	) -> String {
641	    // Gemma-supplied routes; empty when Gemma has not yet run.
642	    let mut routes = routes.to_vec();
643	    let mut seen_tags: HashSet<String> = routes.iter().map(|r| r.tag.clone()).collect();
644	
645	    // Merge legacy UNIX_SOCKET_ENDPOINTS entries for backward compatibility.
646	    for socket in sockets {
647	        let tag = socket.label.clone();
648	        if seen_tags.contains(&tag) {
649	            continue;
650	        }
651	        seen_tags.insert(tag.clone());
652	        routes.push(XrayRoute {
653	            tag,
654	            subdomains: vec![socket.domain.clone()],
655	            backend: GemmaBackend::Unix {
656	                path: socket.path.clone(),
657	            },
658	        });
659	    }
660	
661	    // Outbound for each route that has a backend (ingress tags have none).
662	    let route_outbounds: String = routes
663	        .iter()
664	        .filter_map(|r| route_to_outbound(footprint, trace_id, r))
665	        .collect();
666	
667	    // Subdomain routing rules for each route with subdomains and a real backend.
668	    // Ingress-only entries (e.g. xray-tls/xray-reality) describe the listener,
669	    // not a destination, so no routing rule is emitted for them.
670	    let route_rules: String = routes
671	        .iter()
672	        .filter_map(|r| {
673	            if r.subdomains.is_empty() || matches!(r.backend, GemmaBackend::Ingress) {
674	                return None;
675	            }
676	            let domains = r
677	                .subdomains
678	                .iter()
679	                .map(|d| format!("\"full:{d}\""))
680	                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
681	                .join(", ");
682	            Some(format!(
683	                r#",
684	      {{ "type": "field", "inboundTag": ["op-tls", "ghostbridge-reality"], "domain": [{domains}], "outboundTag": "to-{tag}" }}"#,
685	                tag = r.tag,
686	                domains = domains,
687	            ))
688	        })
689	        .collect();
690	
691	    // Fallback bridge outbound if Gemma did not provide it.
692	    let fallback_outbound = if seen_tags.contains("grpc-bridge") {
693	        String::new()
694	    } else {
695	        format!(

697	    {{
698	      "tag": "to-grpc-bridge",
699	      "protocol": "freedom",
700	      "settings": {{ "redirect": "{host}:{port}" }},
701	      "streamSettings": {{
702	        "network": "xhttp",
703	        "sockopt": {{ "tcpNoDelay": true, "mark": 255 }},
704	        "xhttpSettings": {{
705	          "host": "{host}",
706	          "path": "/Ghostbridge.StateSync",

708	        }}
709	      }}
710	    }}"#,
711	            host = GRPC_BRIDGE_HOST,
712	            port = GRPC_BRIDGE_PORT,
713	        )
714	    };
715	
716	    // Final catch-all fallback to the bridge.
717	    let fallback_rule = if seen_tags.contains("grpc-bridge") {
718	        String::from(
719	            r#",
720	      {
721	        "type": "field",
722	        "inboundTag": ["op-tls", "ghostbridge-reality"],
723	        "outboundTag": "to-grpc-bridge"

725	        )

728	    };

"Direct-dial surface" just means: a way for a WireGuard client to connect straight to 3tched's public IP (`148.113.204.83:51823`) instead of going through the oracle decoy VPS first.

In this design, oracle is supposed to be the *only* front door — it holds the public handshake, and only after that does traffic reach 3tched over the backhaul tunnel. But 3tched's `opdbus` WG interface was also configured with a peer (`OpczuI…`) that had no fixed endpoint — meaning it was waiting to accept a connection dialed straight at 3tched's own public IP, bypassing oracle entirely. That's a second, undocumented entry point into the same network — exactly the "theater" the decoy architecture is supposed to eliminate (a public-facing hole that exists but isn't the sanctioned path).

It was dead anyway (handshake always `0`, nobody actually used it), so I removed that peer entry outright rather than just relying on the firewall to block it.

10	On this Artix box, `s6 set commit` (s6-frontend) compiles a new db AND garbage-collects the old compiled db **even though `/etc/s6/rc/compiled` (the `bootdb` per `s6-frontend.conf`) still hardlinks it by full path**. If `s6 live install` doesn't immediately follow (e.g. it fails on a lock), you're left with: dangling `bootdb` (reboot can fail), and `/run/s6-rc/state` keyed to the now-gone db so `s6-rc` reports "unable to read valid state". Running services are UNAFFECTED — s6-svscan supervises them independently; only the s6-rc management/boot layer breaks.
11	
12	**Always do `s6 set commit` and `s6 live install` back-to-back.** The window between them is the hazard. Use `sudo s6-apply` (`/usr/local/bin/s6-apply`) — the wrapper that does sync→commit→live install atomically, keeps bootdb synced to the live db, rolls bootdb back on failure, and verifies state read afterward. Don't run `s6 set commit` by hand. (The individual `s6` subcommands can't be removed — they're built into the frontend binary — so s6-apply is convention, not enforcement.)
13	
14	**Recovery when the old db is already pruned (validated, no service disruption):**
15	1. Preserve the new db to a stable path outside `/etc/s6/repo/compiled` gc scope: `cp -a <repo/compiled/current> /etc/s6/manualdb/<name>`.
16	2. Reconstruct an old-equiv db: `s6 set mask <newsvcs>` (NOT `disable` — disable keeps them in the db; only `mask` removes from db) → `s6 set commit`. Deterministic compile reproduces the lost db's numbering.

18	4. Dry-run `s6-rc-update -n -v2 -l /run/s6-rc <preserved-new-db>` — confirm stop-list and start-list are EMPTY (no disruption), then run for real.
19	5. Point `bootdb` -> preserved new db. Reconcile frontend: `s6 set unmask` + `s6 set enable` + `s6 set commit`.
20	
21	Keeping boot/live on the stable `/etc/s6/manualdb` copy (not `repo/compiled/current`) makes it immune to future commit gc. See [[artix-s6-layout]]. New service installed this way: zeroclaw-gui-srv/-log (see [[project_zeroclaw_gui_service]]).

---
name: project_s6_commit_prune_hazard
description: "s6-frontend `s6 set commit` prunes the live-referenced compiled db, dangling bootdb; safe recovery procedure"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: baf4e3ab-78a3-4629-beb2-c492ee37aa7b
---

On this Artix box, `s6 set commit` (s6-frontend) compiles a new db AND garbage-collects the old compiled db **even though `/etc/s6/rc/compiled` (the `bootdb` per `s6-frontend.conf`) still hardlinks it by full path**. If `s6 live install` doesn't immediately follow (e.g. it fails on a lock), you're left with: dangling `bootdb` (reboot can fail), and `/run/s6-rc/state` keyed to the now-gone db so `s6-rc` reports "unable to read valid state". Running services are UNAFFECTED — s6-svscan supervises them independently; only the s6-rc management/boot layer breaks.

**Always do `s6 set commit` and `s6 live install` back-to-back.** The window between them is the hazard. Use `sudo s6-apply` (`/usr/local/bin/s6-apply`) — the wrapper that does sync→commit→live install atomically, keeps bootdb synced to the live db, rolls bootdb back on failure, and verifies state read afterward. Don't run `s6 set commit` by hand. (The individual `s6` subcommands can't be removed — they're built into the frontend binary — so s6-apply is convention, not enforcement.)

**Recovery when the old db is already pruned (validated, no service disruption):**
1. Preserve the new db to a stable path outside `/etc/s6/repo/compiled` gc scope: `cp -a <repo/compiled/current> /etc/s6/manualdb/<name>`.
2. Reconstruct an old-equiv db: `s6 set mask <newsvcs>` (NOT `disable` — disable keeps them in the db; only `mask` removes from db) → `s6 set commit`. Deterministic compile reproduces the lost db's numbering.
3. Point `/etc/s6/rc/compiled` -> old-equiv. READ-ONLY VALIDATE: `s6-rc -a list` must read state AND up/down must match ground truth (`s6-svstat` each `/run/s6-rc/servicedirs/*`). Mismatch → abort.
4. Dry-run `s6-rc-update -n -v2 -l /run/s6-rc <preserved-new-db>` — confirm stop-list and start-list are EMPTY (no disruption), then run for real.
5. Point `bootdb` -> preserved new db. Reconcile frontend: `s6 set unmask` + `s6 set enable` + `s6 set commit`.

Keeping boot/live on the stable `/etc/s6/manualdb` copy (not `repo/compiled/current`) makes it immune to future commit gc. See [[artix-s6-layout]]. New service installed this way: zeroclaw-gui-srv/-log (see [[project_zeroclaw_gui_service]]).

- Same failure mode as 2026-06-19's "assistant :18789 not running" recurred: an s6-rc db compiled+swapped in at 03:01 added `op-grpc-bridge`, `op-cognitive-mcp`, `zeroclaw`, `op-web-srv`, `wg-netmaker`, `netmaker-rumqttd`, `op-grpc-bridge-zeroclaw` with `down` files and never brought them up — s6-supervise was running (babysitting) but nothing had sent the "up" signal. This silently broke ALL xray subdomain routing (every backend port was dead). Fixed live via `s6-svc -u "$live_servicedir"` on each (safe/reversible — starting an idle supervised service). **Not yet persisted**: only the live `/run/s6-rc:*` tree was touched; the source servicedir `down` files still need removing so a reboot doesn't regress. When routing "mysteriously" breaks again, check `s6-svstat` on the live servicedirs for `down (not started yet)` before assuming an xray config bug.
- **Confirmed NOT a bug** (don't re-flag): `schema_bridge.rs`'s `GemmaBackend::Unix` route-to-outbound handling discards the socket `path` and redirects to `GRPC_BRIDGE_HOST:GRPC_BRIDGE_PORT` (`10.200.0.1:50051`) instead. This is intentional per the doc comment at `schema_bridge.rs:472` — unix-backed routes (cognitive-mcp, netmaker-api) go through the grpc-bridge's gRPC-reflection demux, not a direct xray domainsocket outbound. `10.200.0.1:50051` has a real live listener; this path works correctly once the bridge is up.
- **Real remaining gap**: qdrant and netmaker-ui/netmaker-api containers run in their own Incus network namespace, so xray's plain `TCP 127.0.0.1:<port>` outbounds (qdrant 6333, netmaker-ui 8081) can never reach them from the host namespace — confirmed qdrant really is listening on 6333/6334 but only inside its own netns. These need the same UDS treatment cognitive-mcp already has (`unix_socket` plugin → grpc-bridge demux), not a port-number fix.

---
name: xray-router
description: "xray is the main router — OpenFlow tag-based routing, nginx/subdomain forwarder; oracle ingress is a decoy; xray config must be dynamic; next step is adding Gemma to the xray router stack"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0ef14d6e-2b10-4e31-965d-7402203c5317
---

xray (the xraqy identity layer, see [[identity-injection]]) is the **main router** of the network: it does OpenFlow tag-based routing and serves as the nginx / subdomain forwarder. The oracle (cloud) ingress is a decoy — real traffic decisions happen in xray.

The xray config must be **dynamic, not static** (Factory sessions, June 2026). Plan from those sessions:
- `op-identity/src/schema_bridge.rs` already writes `/dev/shm/xray-ghostbridge.json` — xray config generated from the identity sled (sled lives in SHM, is a ledger of everything the session touches, and drives tag-based routing + ghostbridge header injection).
- Replace the hardcoded Rust template: generate xray config from D-Bus plugin tree + sled state. Flow: sled mutation → D-Bus call to zeroclaw plugin → **Gemma** (ollama, already installed, reachable via zeroclaw plugin / `zeroclaw_chat` through cognitive-mcp CallTool) outputs the xray JSON config. This is how Gemma joins the router stack.
- xray dynamically creates per-socket inbounds/outbounds/routing rules (TLS+Reality inbounds, gRPC outbounds, native unix-socket support); auto-generates TLS certs.
- Hypervisor stack: xray server, OVS, netclient, ofcontroller — all dumb; xray+Gemma do the OpenFlow tag-based routing. Option: two controller tables — OVS controller for domain routing only, xray the rest.
- Requirements: tonic reflection + tonic TLS everywhere. Pending deploys from that session: op-identity with new xray template, op-grpc-bridge with tonic TLS.
- Old VPS contract ended 2026-06-12; xray server already moved to hypervisor; gateway will sit on a decoy VPS connecting back to wg-xray; wg-xray no longer needs nic-type=physical isolation (can be routed/bridged). Netmaker egress was done with 10.0.0.1 only.

**State 2026-06-12 (this session):**
- Fresh binaries built+deployed to /usr/local/bin: op-identity-sled, op-grpc-bridge (TLS done in code — env GRPC_TLS_CERT/KEY or rcgen self-signed + ServerTlsConfig), op-xray-daemon. None run as services yet.
- PATH VIOLATION FIXED 2026-06-12: op-xray-daemon now serves at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/xray` (was off-tree `/opdbus/v1/xray`); caller in schema_bridge.rs updated to match; xray.rs oscal_source literal fixed to /org prefix. Rebuilt+deployed. (Bus name still `opdbus.v1`; daemon still a standalone process rather than folded into the mirror-projected plugin — acceptable since the rule is about the object PATH. Deeper fold-into-plugin deferred.)
- Generator rewrite: subdomain→socket routing (drop per-socket TCP inbounds; SocketEntry = label:path:subdomain; route by sniffed SNI into freedom/ds outbounds). Split into testable pure build_xray_config. 2 tests pass.
- Dynamic pipeline (run_schema_shuttle: read sled → write /dev/shm/xray-ghostbridge.json → start xray via D-Bus opdbus.v1.Xray.start → watch_wireguard_handshakes) is coded but NOT wired at runtime. Live xray still runs as plain s6 service `gbr-xray`/`xray` off STATIC /etc/xray/config.json (valid vless REALITY egress — don't break it).
- **BLOCKER for live cutover:** no /etc/ghostbridge/xray.env — missing XRAY_UUID / XRAY_PRIVATE_KEY / XRAY_SHORT_ID / NEXTDNS_PROFILE_ID (were on old VPS, mid-migration). Without them the generator can't produce the shm config. Also need op-xray-daemon running + registered on system bus (opdbus.v1 /opdbus/v1/xray) before the shuttle's D-Bus start works.
- Netmaker egress DONE this session: netmaker mesh (100.90.37.0/24) → opdbus via iptables FORWARD + MASQUERADE, persisted in /etc/iptables/rules.v4 (restored by s6 iptables-restore). 10.0.0.2 reachable. Local netmaker server container can't run (broker token timeout — broker/api on decoy 129.153.134.63; api.ghostbridge.tech serves ZeroClaw UI not raw netmaker API), so egress done via direct iptables not dashboard.

**State 2026-06-19 (xray migrated to HOST):**
- **NO nginx anywhere** (user-confirmed) — xray itself is the subdomain forwarder. Two mechanisms in one config: (1) VLESS `op-tls` inbound on 443 with an SNI `fallbacks` table (plain-browser HTTPS → dest port by SNI) and (2) `routing.rules` with `domain:` matchers (tunnel traffic → freedom/redirect outbounds). SNI sniffing `routeOnly:true`.
- **xray now runs ON THE HOST**, not in the `wg-xray` container. Cutover this session: the public edge had been forwarded into `wg-xray` by Incus proxy devices (`port-443` = `listen 0.0.0.0:443 → connect 127.0.0.1:443`, plus mail port-25/143/465/587/993). Domain forwarding was fully DOWN (all subdomains HTTP 000) because **no `xray run` process existed anywhere** — the host `xray` s6 service was `down` + not in the `default` bundle, and nothing ran in the container.
- **Fix applied:** edited `/etc/xray/config.json` op-tls `listen` 10.0.0.2 → **0.0.0.0**; `sudo incus config device remove wg-xray port-443` (freed host 443; reversible, mail port devices left intact so mail still ingresses via the container); removed `/etc/s6/sv/xray/down`; `sudo s6 set enable xray`; `sudo bash deploy/s6/recompile-and-update.sh`; `sudo s6 live start xray`. Now xray is active, bound `*:443`, in default bundle (boot-persistent). Verified `qdrant.ghostbridge.tech → HTTP 200` end-to-end.
- `incus` CLI as user `jeremy` (group `wheel`, not `incus`) gets "permission denied" on the socket — must use **`sudo incus`**. The socket is `root:incus`.
- The host `/etc/xray/config.json` is now the authoritative ingress config. `gbr-xray` is a SEPARATE service (REALITY egress for the privacy chain) — don't conflate. The container's `/etc/xray/config.json` (via `/proc/<initpid>/root/...`) is now legacy.
- **SNI-dispatcher architecture (h2 vs http/1.1 split):** xray fallback is a raw passthrough — it can't bridge an h2-negotiating browser to an http/1.1-only backend. qdrant.* is gRPC (REQUIRES h2); netmaker web UIs (dashboard/netmaker-ui, op-web) are http/1.1-only and break if the browser negotiates h2. Solution on `:443`: a `dokodemo-door` **`sni-dispatch`** inbound (no TLS termination, `sniffing destOverride:[tls] routeOnly`) peeks the ClientHello SNI and routes (freedom `redirect`) to one of two internal loopback VLESS+TLS inbounds — **`tls-h2` 127.0.0.1:8444** (ALPN `["h2","http/1.1"]`, fallback → qdrant 6334) and **`tls-h1` 127.0.0.1:8445** (ALPN `["http/1.1"]` only, fallbacks → all web backends, default op-web 8080). qdrant.* → to-h2; everything else → to-h1. ghostbridge-reality:8443 unchanged. Also a plaintext **`http-80`** dokodemo inbound on `:80` sniffs the HTTP `Host` header (`destOverride:[http]`) and routes to the same web backends (no TLS) so `http://<subdomain>` works over the internal mesh (subdomains resolve to 10.200.0.2). Internal DNS points `*.ghostbridge.tech` at 10.200.0.2 (mesh), not the public IP 148.113.204.83.
- **Fallback dest gotcha:** bare-port fallback `dest` (e.g. `28081`) makes xray dial `localhost` → tries **IPv6 `[::1]`** first, but the Incus forkproxies listen **IPv4 `127.0.0.1` only** → "connection refused". Always write fallback dest as explicit `"127.0.0.1:<port>"`.
- Backends still down (separate from forwarding, 2026-06-19): `assistant` :18789 (ghostbridge gRPC bridge, not running); `netmaker` API container crash-loops on LXC mount error `Failed to mount "none" onto "/usr/lib/lxc/rootfs/run"` (netmaker-ui + netmaker-mq containers DO stay up).

Related: [[zero-trust-principle]], [[mcp-grpc-transport]], [[identity-injection]], [[3tched-architecture]].

input.content:
---
name: project_oracle_decoy_relay_asbuilt
description: "Oracle VPS decoy ingress is already a live WG-terminating hub with TCP DNAT to 3tched — not a dumb relay; direct-dial peers on 3tched bypassing it are unwanted theater, remove them"
metadata:
  type: project
  originSessionId: 97cad471-0bad-477d-821b-560a1c9e8d61
---

As-built (confirmed live 2026-07-07, 57GB+ transferred, long-running): the Oracle Always-Free VM (`129.153.134.63`, OCI instance `decoy-wg2`, OS Ubuntu 24.04, user `ubuntu`) runs a full WireGuard hub, **not** a dumb UDP relay:

- `wg0` on port 51821, oracle pubkey `6mx4ycJeDMEDUknDY+sVlus1PQOEGG9/XrGFBuB1GFY=`, address `10.0.0.1/24` (+ legacy `10.189.0.1/24`).
- Peers: 3tched itself (`iNqgBk7pBC/iXUmF+v4PNvvdAxjP5qWjxzMYYRE8+hw=`, `10.0.0.2/32`) and real clients (e.g. a laptop/router at `10.0.0.3/32`, endpoint = the client's real public IP).
- `iptables-nft` PREROUTING DNATs public TCP ports (80, 443, 3003, 18789, 50051, 50052, mail ports, 8443) from `ens3` to `10.0.0.2:<port>` over the WG tunnel; FORWARD chain scopes exactly those ports; POSTROUTING masquerades.
- This means WG **terminates at oracle** (not end-to-end to 3tched) for the TCP dataplane. Identity chain reasoning from `[[project_container_identity_is_sessionid]]`/`[[project_key_derivation]]` about "relay preserves end-to-end WG identity" turned out moot — termination-at-oracle is what's actually deployed and has been working for a long time. Don't re-litigate relay-vs-terminate; this is settled/as-built.
- `~/.ssh/vps_key` on 3tched authenticates to oracle as user `ubuntu` (not `jeremy`/`opc`/`root`) — `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` does NOT work there. OCI CLI is configured (`~/.oci/config`) and can list instances/enumerate the public IP when SSH access is in question.

**Direct-dial peers on 3tched's own `opdbus` interface are theater, remove them.** A peer with no `Endpoint` (waiting for the client to dial 3tched's public IP directly, bypassing oracle) defeats the "oracle is the only front door" design — confirmed by user as intentional to eliminate, not a design they wanted kept. Found and removed one (`OpczuI5c0ckPnNMTjhP3B9awoxZJTDwJHnRAsv1AEhM=`, dead/unused, handshake always 0) 2026-07-07. When adding new clients, add them as a peer of **oracle's `wg0` hub** (get a `10.0.0.x/32` slot there, `AllowedIPs=10.0.0.0/24` on the client side pointed at `129.153.134.63:51821`), never as a second direct peer on 3tched's own opdbus listener.

Related: [[project_xray_router]], [[project_container_identity_is_sessionid]].

python3 <<'EOF'
import socket, struct, random

def query(domain, server='8.8.8.8', port=53, timeout=5):
    tid = random.randint(0, 65535)
    header = struct.pack('>HHHHHH', tid, 0x0100, 1, 0, 0, 0)
    qparts = b''.join(struct.pack('B', len(p)) + p.encode() for p in domain.split('.'))
    question = qparts + b'\x00' + struct.pack('>HH', 1, 1)  # A, IN
    packet = header + question
    s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    s.settimeout(timeout)
    try:
        s.sendto(packet, (server, port))
        data, _ = s.recvfrom(512)
    except Exception as e:
        return f"ERR {e}"
    finally:
        s.close()
    ancount = struct.unpack('>H', data[6:8])[0]
    if ancount == 0:
        return "NXDOMAIN/no answer"
    # crude parse: skip to answers after question section
    idx = 12
    while data[idx] != 0:
        idx += data[idx] + 1
    idx += 5  # null + qtype + qclass
    ips = []
    for _ in range(ancount):
        # name (likely pointer 2 bytes)
        if data[idx] & 0xC0 == 0xC0:
            idx += 2
        else:
            while data[idx] != 0:
                idx += data[idx] + 1
            idx += 1
        rtype, rclass, ttl, rdlen = struct.unpack('>HHIH', data[idx:idx+10])
        idx += 10
        rdata = data[idx:idx+rdlen]
        if rtype == 1 and rdlen == 4:
            ips.append('.'.join(str(b) for b in rdata))
        idx += rdlen
    return ips or "no A record"

for d in ["ghostbridge.tech","assistant.ghostbridge.tech","api.ghostbridge.tech","qdrant.ghostbridge.tech","dashboard.ghostbridge.tech","broker.ghostbridge.tech","cozo.ghostbridge.tech","mail.3tched.com","3tched.com"]:
    print(d, "->", query(d))
EOF

content.text:
DNS is actually fine — I verified with a raw query against `8.8.8.8`: every subdomain (`ghostbridge.tech`, `assistant.*`, `api.*`, `qdrant.*`, `dashboard.*`, `broker.*`, `cozo.*`, `mail.3tched.com`) correctly resolves to oracle's public IP `129.153.134.63`. That's correct by design — public clients hit oracle, oracle DNATs into the tunnel, xray on 3tched then routes by SNI. Locally on 3tched, `/etc/hosts` shortcuts everything to `10.0.0.2` (itself) for efficiency, which is also fine.

So the real remaining gap is exactly what I flagged before: **qdrant and netmaker-ui containers aren't reachable from xray's namespace once traffic arrives.** Let me wire those properly using the mandated `unix_socket` plugin instead of the broken raw TCP redirect.

content.text:
I found the actual reason qdrant/netmaker-ui are unreachable, and it raises an architecture question I shouldn't just decide on my own.

Confirmed: `qdrant`'s process (PID 3618) is genuinely inside its own container network namespace (`lxc.payload.qdrant`, netns `4026532441` vs. host's `4026531833`) — that's why `curl 127.0.0.1:6333` from the host fails even though qdrant is healthy inside its container. The container's Incus config has zero devices (`devices: {}`) — no proxy, no socket passthrough, nothing bridges it to the host.

The catch: the `unix_socket` plugin (the CLAUDE.md-mandated way to expose container sockets) is **specifically for our own gRPC-reflectable services** — its own doc comment says it "neither opens these ports nor maps them... tonic-web demuxes by reflection." Qdrant is third-party (its own REST/gRPC, not reflection-compatible with our bridge), so that plugin mechanism doesn't actually apply to it. The only two paths I see:

questions.question: Qdrant/netmaker-ui are third-party services that don't speak our gRPC-reflection demux, so the unix_socket plugin's mechanism doesn't cover them. How should I bridge them from their container netns to xray on the host?

options.label: Incus proxy device (Recommended)
options.description: Add a proxy device (host 127.0.0.1:6333 → container qdrant:6333, same for netmaker-ui). No NIC/IP assigned to the container — Incus proxy devices work via nsenter socket forwarding, not routing. This is what the June session likely used before it was removed.

options.label: Extend unix_socket plugin for raw TCP
options.description: Add a real passthrough mode to the unix_socket plugin for non-reflectable backends, so third-party containers get the same sanctioned path as our own services. More work, but keeps everything on one mechanism.

options.label: Leave qdrant/netmaker-ui unreachable for now
options.description: Skip fixing these two; they may not be in active use yet (netmaker appliance work is parked per earlier notes). Revisit later.

content.text:
To be clear — the code already uses **tonic's** TLS API (`tonic::transport::{Identity, ServerTlsConfig}`), which is the correct, sanctioned approach. Nothing needs to change there.

The panic is one level lower: tonic's TLS support is implemented *using* rustls internally (that's how tonic works, not a choice we're making). Rustls 0.23 requires a process picks exactly one crypto backend (`ring` or `aws-lc-rs`) and calls `CryptoProvider::install_default()` once at startup — and because more than one of those backend crates ends up in the dependency tree (pulled in transitively by different deps), rustls can't guess which one to use, so it panics instead of silently picking wrong.

The fix is a one-line addition at the top of `main()` in `op-grpc-bridge.rs` — install the default crypto provider before the TLS server is built. It doesn't touch how we call tonic's TLS API at all. Want me to add that?

content.text:
Confirmed — the exhook integration is real code, but genuinely half-wired:

- **Our side is ready**: `op-grpc-bridge` already implements and serves `emqx_exhook.HookProvider` (`emqx_hook_provider.rs`) as part of its normal gRPC server on port 18789 — EMQX would call *this* for every MQTT connect/publish/disconnect event, logged through MutationEngine for accountability.
- **EMQX's side is not configured at all.** I checked `netmaker-pro`'s live EMQX config (`/etc/emqx/base.hocon`, `emqx.conf`) — there's no `exhook.servers` stanza anywhere, only the stock example file (`exhook.conf.example`) showing the format (`url = "http://127.0.0.1:9090"` style). The hook was never actually pointed at our service.
- **There's a real network snag if we just point it at op-grpc-bridge as-is**: `op-grpc-bridge` binds loopback-only (`127.0.0.1:18789`) on 3tched, and its normal ingress path is xray's VLESS listener on 443/8443 — but EMQX's exhook client is a plain gRPC-over-TLS client, not VLESS-aware, so it can't tunnel through that ingress the way normal traffic does. It would need either a direct route to `10.0.0.2:18789` over the WG mesh (if `netmaker-pro` even has WG connectivity — unclear, it showed a separate public IP `15.235.37.41`) or a dedicated plain-TLS port exposed just for this purpose.

That last part is a real design decision, not something I should just wire up unilaterally. How do you want EMQX to reach the hook service — over WG mesh, a separate exposed port, or something else you already have in mind?

Traced it further — the WG-mesh path is the right target architecturally, but it doesn't exist yet:

- 3tched's `netclient` (`wg-netmaker` service) has **no active network membership** — its own config (`/etc/netclient/netclient.json`) shows `"nodes": null`. 
- Its last real registration attempt (from logs dated 2026-07-04) was against a **stale cloud SaaS Netmaker server** (`a453a2c7-....app.prod.netmaker.io`), not the self-hosted `netmaker-pro` container — and that was failing with 404/auth errors even then.
- So 3tched isn't meshed with `netmaker-pro` at all right now. Restarting the daemon just re-armed the interface with no peers (matches the empty `wg show netmaker` I saw earlier).

To actually join 3tched to `netmaker-pro`'s network (so `10.x.x.x` reaches it, and op-grpc-bridge could bind an address on that mesh for EMQX's exhook calls), `netclient` needs a fresh **enrollment token** generated from `netmaker-pro`'s own server/API — I don't have one, and generating it means calling into `netmaker-pro`'s admin API (port 8081, or via its dashboard/caddy front). Do you have an enrollment token already, or want me to try generating one from the netmaker-pro API directly (I have shell access into that container)?

The actual protocol termination (and, critically, the **ghostbridge identity header injection** — `x-ghostbridge-footprint`/`x-ghostbridge-trace-id`, sourced from the identity sled at `/dev/shm/plugin_schema.dat` **on 3tched**) happens on 3tched's own xray, locally, after the encrypted bytes arrive unmodified via DNAT.

If oracle becomes the actual VLESS/REALITY-terminating server, oracle is now the one that would need to inject those headers — but the sled state (mutation_index, schema catalog hash, footprint) is 3tched-local memory. Oracle can't compute the same footprint without either (a) replicating sled-read logic across the WG link, or (b) the interceptor on 3tched being changed to trust something oracle *can* legitimately assert (e.g. the WG pubkey alone) instead of a footprint oracle can't compute.

This isn't a blocker, just something I don't want to quietly paper over. Do you want oracle to:
1. Terminate VLESS/REALITY fully (server role complete), and we adjust the 3tched-side interceptor to accept identity from oracle differently, or
2. Still just pass through the *encrypted* session to 3tched for real termination (i.e., keep today's DNAT model, and "xray on oracle" means something narrower — like just the REALITY-cloaked egress/client piece we were discussing before, not full server termination)?

I've exhausted the reasonable debugging paths here without success. Summary of what I ruled out, definitively:

- **Not the keys** — tested with a completely fresh, independently-generated X25519 keypair; same failure.
- **Not oracle-specific** — reproduced identically against 3tched's own local REALITY server, isolated on loopback.
- **Not VLESS/UUID auth** — plain VLESS with no TLS/REALITY works perfectly (`200 OK`).
- **Not the new ML-DSA-65 post-quantum fields** — added `mldsa65Seed`/`mldsa65Verify`; no change.

Every REALITY handshake attempt fails identically with `"handshake did not complete successfully"`, regardless of client/server pairing, on this exact xray version (26.3.27). This looks like it could be a genuine bug or undocumented breaking change in this specific build's REALITY implementation — something I can't resolve further without either internet access to check the Xray-core changelog/issues for this version, or a known-good reference client to compare against, neither of which I have here.

Given how much ground we've covered already today, I think this is the right place to stop rather than keep guessing blindly at REALITY's internals. Options from here:
1. Try downloading a different (older or newer) xray-core release and see if REALITY works there instead.
2. Drop REALITY for the egress path specifically and use something simpler (plain TLS to oracle, still hides traffic shape from casual inspection just not full REALITY camouflage).
3. Pause here for today — everything else from today's session (s6 services, DNS, op-grpc-bridge crash fix, qdrant/zeroclaw routing, WG cleanup, OVH IP relocation) is solid and unaffected by this.
